title: Binary function under a fixed restriction
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f$ be a function from the sign cube $\\{−1,1\\}^n$ to $\\{−1,1\\}$, let $J\\subseteq\\{1,\\ldots,n\\}$, and fix signs on the coordinates outside $J$. The associated function on the binary cube $\\mathbb F_2^n$ sends each binary input to its sign-cube encoding, extends the fixed signs on the coordinates outside $J$, and evaluates $f$ on the resulting sign vector.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a Boolean function on $n$ sign coordinates
$J$ is a finite set of indices in $\\mathrm{Fin}(n)$
a sign assignment is fixed on indices outside $J$
caveat: The formal statement relies on the omitted definitions of the sign embedding, binary-cube sign equivalence, and extended sign restriction; the prose describes their apparent construction.
